description: Two-wheeled walking tractor with long steering handlebars towing a flatbed trailer, used for farm hauling and short road trips.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Two-wheeled walking tractor with an exposed single-cylinder diesel engine over a pair of large lugged wheels, long twin steering handlebars swept back, hitched to a flatbed wooden trailer on two wheels with low stake sides Materials: Bare and rusted steel frame, oil-blackened engine block, mud packed into the lugged tyre treads, sun-greyed and split trailer planks, flaking bright enamel on the engine cowl.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 3,840/4,000 triangles, 4/4 draw calls, 3/3 materials, 4/6 unique geometries, two canvases at 1.7 MB, factory 51 ms. Turntable: enclosed background is the open frame between the bars and under the trailer, allowed on measurement (holeviz: no surface flagged).

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 1.56 x 1.35 x 4.23 m against a declared 1.50 x 1.35 x 4.20 (trailer wheels and tail stakes, inside the 0.1 tolerance); stations off the proxy side elevation (engine 0.02-0.22 L, drive wheel 0.10-0.30 L, bars to 0.55 L at 1.00 H, trailer 0.55-0.98 L, trailer wheels 0.78 L). The raked column now carries the bars from the gearbox as the plate shows, and the 090/270 frames match the plate's tank-below-board-top relationship.
featureReviews.notes: The proxy is 2.56 lengths tall against the real 3.11; heights are its fractions of H.

featureReviews.evidence: Fan drum with grille disc and crank boss on the left end, block over the crankcase, four-fin head with a silver rocker cover, air-cleaner box, muffler, belt cover, injector pump with its fuel line, red tank with filler cap and the red column raked 0.54 rad to a junction bracket; bars from the junction with a cross tube, stays, clutch lever, throttle cable and grips; full U bumper loop and crank handle. Red authored as the probed inverse of the plate's shaded tank (#86302a) and renders #b6433d lit.
featureReviews.notes: No hoses, labels or bolt heads; the engine is the plate's massing at prop distance, not its plumbing.

featureReviews.evidence: Deck, three separate plank courses a side with 2 cm daylight, three head and two tail planks, ten proud rust-steel stakes, steel chassis channels and cross members and the steel A-frame with cross brace and hitch eye on the pin; plank canvas as map and bump; wood at #958d85 renders #756a5c on the side against the plate's #7a7066.
featureReviews.notes: The trailer wheel dish has no vent holes.

featureReviews.evidence: Two instanced 0.84 m drive wheels with eighteen chevron lugs merged into the lathe on rust-red dishes with hub caps; two 0.56 m black trailer wheels on steel dishes merged into the trim; pivots wheel-l/r, trailer-wheel-l/r and hitch.
featureReviews.notes: Lugs read at every azimuth; the sidewall is smooth.

name: Iron Buffalo Walking Tractor
notes: Declared as the tractor plus its trailer together, which is how it is always seen on a road -- the tractor alone is a bare engine on two wheels and reads as a machine part rather than a vehicle. That is why the 4.2 m length. The trailer really does unhitch, but it is left out of destructionGroups because destruction groups are for assemblies the prop breaks into, not for a working hitch; if a consumer needs the trailer separate it should be its own asset.
